transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hi there! Do you have any questions about your cataract surgery or recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi! Yes, I do have a few questions. Firstly, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
You should avoid any exercise for 1 week after surgery, but you can then go back to light exercise, such as brisk walking, gardening, light jogging, and gentle cycling. You should avoid strenuous, heavy exercise, lifting heavy objects, pilates or yoga, or swimming for a month.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Great, thanks for letting me know. Next, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
If you were using any eye drops before your operation, such as for glaucoma or for dry eyes, it's safe to continue using them, unless you've been told otherwise.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That’s good to hear. Another thing, I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to the new lenses. However, significant pain when it's bright or severe light sensitivity is not normal, especially if your eye is also red and painful, and we may need to assess this further. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, we'd recommend just wearing sunglasses when you go outside.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for clarifying that. Lastly, should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's common for your vision to not be completely clear in the first week after your operation. This should improve quickly and settle down over time. If your vision is still blurry, or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure it’s okay.

If we put in a standard lens, it’s common to have difficulty reading as most lenses are for distance vision. This means you will need reading glasses, or varifocals for reading, and that’s entirely normal if it’s the only part of your vision that is blurry. Unfortunately, I don’t have access to your medical records, so I don’t know what lens was used.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, that's all my questions for now. Thank you so much for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're welcome! Just to confirm, have all your questions been answered?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, you've answered all my questions. Thank you again!
